hook_text: Raise the taxi fare and the till fills. Raise the chips price and it empties. Same street. Why?
clip_script: Some prices you can sidestep; others you must swallow. Your favourite chips go up two rand — you shrug and grab the rival brand. Your demand stretched like a rubber band. The taxi fare to school goes up two rand — you grumble, you pay, you ride. That demand is a plank; planks do not bend. And the stretch forecasts the till: push up a plank's price and the till swells — the riders still ride. Push up a rubber band's price and the till shrinks — customers scatter faster than the higher price can pay back. Now run your own vetkoek stall. The going price is fifteen rand, every single one. So interrogate only the NEXT vetkoek: while it costs less than fifteen to make, fry it. The morning it costs more — the oil overworked, the helper on overtime — stop. Economists call that marginal revenue equals marginal cost. It is really just a cook who counts honestly.
visual_style: A price tag bouncing off a stretched rubber band, then knocking flat against a plank; a till gauge rising and falling; a vetkoek pan sliding out golden rounds while a cost meter climbs toward fifteen and a spatula halts the pan at the line.
mood: Street-smart and playful, tightening into one clean rule.
pacing: Snappy alternating beats for band and plank, a slower sizzle through the vetkoek count, hard stop on the rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep: three kitchens, four envelopes, the national till slip and the two drivers.
